A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison: 30 of 33 pages render identically, and the remaining differences are identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments, including 2,968 Turing-test judgments from 397 participants, human-likeness annotations, and evaluations of the proposed AI judge, with additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original human evaluation, annotation analyses, AI-judge experiments, and appendix results. These remain original empirical outcomes produced by the work.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-Omni evaluator, fused representation, Ordinal Discretization Layer, training objectives, and regularized linear classifier are unchanged in Section 6.2 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English and Chinese human–human, human–machine, and pseudo-human dialogues. Coverage of CosyVoice2, Fisher, and MultiDialog in out-of-domain evaluation is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the nine automated judges in Table 2, Qwen2.5-Omni and its LoRA variant plus human judges in Table 3, and the appendix ablation comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, preprocessing, dialogue-generation strategies, evaluation metrics, training settings, and testing procedures are identical. Both versions evaluate 64 dialogues from each out-of-domain dataset.

E4.justification: Both retain the same dialogue-length analysis, expert-annotation correction study, representation and module ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, out-of-domain tests, and contribution case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 and Table 16 retain five runs with different random seeds and mean ± standard error reporting. The trend tests in Appendix C.3 and uncertainty reporting elsewhere are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical, including all appendix results. For example, proposed-judge overall accuracy remains 0.9605 in Table 3 and out-of-domain accuracy remains 0.9740 in Table 4.

T1.justification: The ordinal cut-point definitions, cumulative-link probabilities, optimization objectives, regularization, and feature-contribution calculations are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: no evaluated S2S system passes the test, the 18-dimension taxonomy diagnoses human-likeness deficiencies, and the proposed interpretable judge improves discrimination.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning paralinguistic, emotional, and persona deficiencies, automated-judge biases, generalization, and failure cases remain identical. No applicability boundary or substantive limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: Implementation details, prompts, annotation procedures, hyperparameters, hardware, computational costs, and code/data/model access information are unchanged. The funding acknowledgment edit does not alter technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same VoiceBench and MMAU-Pro comparison; Table 5 is relocated without changing its content.

P1.justification: The acknowledgment removes National Natural Science Foundation of China grants 62372058 and U22A2026, retaining the Longgang grant and adjusting the sentence. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 5 moves from the top of page 16, before the final reference and appendix introductory material, to directly after Appendix A's opening paragraph. Page 11 also reflows after the shortened acknowledgment; table contents and other figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Moving Table 5 beside its introducing discussion modestly tidies the presentation. Otherwise, the changes concern funding acknowledgment and version metadata. Methods, empirical support, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
